question:
Which of the following pair of compound name – formula is correct?

I. Calcium oxide – Ca₂O

II. Aluminum Oxide – Al₂O₃
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Calcium oxide (CaO)__, commonly known as quicklime or burnt lime, is a widely used chemical compound.

 
 
• It is a white, caustic, alkaline, crystalline solid at room temperature.
 
• **Formula**: CaO
 
• **IUPAC ID**: Oxocalcium
 
• **Molar mass**: 56.0774 g/mol
 
• **Melting point**: 2,572 °C
 
• **Density**: 3.34 g/cm³​
 
• **Soluble in:** Water, Glycerol.
 
 

***Thus I is incorrect.***

 
• Aluminium oxide is a white odourless crystalline powder. It is water-insoluble.

 
 
• Aluminium oxide has a chemical formula of Al₂O₃.
 
• It is amphoteric in nature and is used in various chemical, industrial and commercial applications.
 
• An oxide of aluminium occurs in nature as various minerals such as bauxite, corundum, etc.
 
• It is used as an adsorbent, desiccating agent, and catalyst, and in the manufacture of dental cement and refractories.
 
 

*Thus II is correct.*
